headline: HSC and equivalent exam results to be published on October 29
summary: The Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee chairman confirmed the date, following a meeting with the education minister and secretary. Further details are expected on October 26.
details: Results of this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will be published on October 29, the Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee chairman has announced.
Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, chair of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dhaka, confirmed this decision was reached on Saturday.

He told bdnews24.com that the decision followed a meeting at the education ministry with the secretary and the education minister. Further details regarding the results will be announced on October 26.

headline_marked: [[Japan eyes Bangladesh to make cars]] with $6.35 billion potential investment
headline: Japan eyes Bangladesh to make cars with $6.35 billion potential investment
summary: Japanese companies, including Toyota, are considering manufacturing cars and parts in Bangladesh, aiming to shift from import reliance to local assembly and eventually full-scale production. This comes as PM Tarique Rahman visits Japan.
details: Japanese companies are exploring investment in car and parts manufacturing in Bangladesh, aiming to reduce reliance on imported Japanese brands. Reports indicate a potential $6.35 billion in Japanese private investment over five years.

The plan involves starting with vehicle assembly using imported components, gradually moving towards full-scale manufacturing. Building a competitive industry will require stronger local supply chains and access to high-quality steel.

Toyota Tsusho Corporation plans a $40 million investment for two sales, servicing, and spare-parts centres in Dhaka and Chattogram. Construction for these facilities is scheduled to begin in November 2026.

Separately, Toyota Tsusho is planning a hybrid electric vehicle manufacturing facility in a National Special Economic Zone. Development is expected to begin in 2027, with full-scale production targeted for 2029.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's upcoming visit to Japan from October 26 to 29 is expected to advance economic cooperation and strengthen strategic ties. This visit comes amid Japan's "China Plus One" policy, which seeks to deepen industrial ties with Bangladesh.

Beyond the auto sector, energy infrastructure and the Matarbari deep-sea port in Cox's Bazar are also identified as significant avenues for Japanese investment. JERA, Japan's largest power generation company, is already involved in an LNG-based power plant in Meghnaghat.

However, challenges remain, including the need for stronger domestic capabilities in steel, chemicals, and precision engineering. Long-term industrial investment also requires predictable regulations and reliable energy supplies.
